subject: research/osrobot-deadlineloss
professional: a programme-committee reviewer at a real-time systems / robotics venue (RTSS, ICRA, or an ASABE machinery-management session) who knows deadline scheduling with tardiness cost and farm-machinery timeliness costing. They would check first: is every person-hour the system needs charged (a drone flight needs a remote pilot), does the cost model actually penalise extra machines bought only to meet a tight window, is the lateness model the standard timeliness-cost form and cited, does the result survive the corrections already made to the parent models, and is the nearest prior work (ASABE EP496/D497 timeliness coefficients, two-stage hybrid flow-shop scheduling with weighted tardiness, robot-weeding economics such as Lowenberg-DeBoer et al. 2020) cited.

evidence.correctness: Ran `PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 experiments/run.py > /tmp/claude-0/dl_results.txt`: every number equals the committed results.txt (the only diff is literal '\n' text, see craft). Independent re-implementation with no subject imports (/tmp/claude-0/dl/indep.py; constants from osrobot-pairprice's printed Sweep 2 fits, scheduler written with lists and a closed form for inline) reproduces the worst cell (pipe 4,6 fleet 12.46 total 21.02; inline 12.27 total 17.80), Sweep 3 (8 h 13.07/12.27, 12 h 11.43/12.27, 24 h 10.91/12.27), the ratio ranges 1.49-1.51 at 0.18 ha and 1.06-1.20 at 0.72 ha, and 13.92 USD/ha for 1 scout + 1 treater. By hand: inline at 1.62 ha busy 3+0.96+227.6*1.62 = 372.7 min; 16 robots: capital 80000*0.3*6.21/500 = 298.2, people 16, energy 3.83 -> 12.27/ha; loss 2.21 h late /8/2 = 0.138 stages * 2% * 2000 * 25.92 ha = 143.3 -> 5.53/ha (matches). The 2% per leaf stage rate matches the Knezevic, Evans & Mainz 2003 abstract (AGRIS record). So the arithmetic is right. But the outputs are of a model that the repository already knows is wrong: the scout pilot is unpaid (README Limitations). Charging the scout's flight minutes at the project's 20 USD/h (as osrobot-pairprice's corrected econ.py does) in the same re-implementation turns the 1.62 ha range from 0.89-1.18 into 2.25-2.71: the 'verdict flips with the window' headline disappears. And capital charged per machine-hour of makespan makes extra inline robots free (C5: 12.27 USD/ha for n = 1, 2, 4, 8, 16), so the deadline trade-off on the inline side is an accounting artefact. Right arithmetic on a known-wrong model: 2.
evidence.completeness: Claimed: 7 tests (ran: 7 OK in 0.002 s); results.txt regenerable in seconds (yes, numbers identical, layout differs); figure parsed from Sweep 3 (figure.py reads only Sweep 3, unaffected); loss model with cap (fleet.py:78-83, tested); search over s<=4, k<=16, n<=32 with fewest-machine tie-break (fleet.py:113-130); Sweeps 1-3 all present; 13.92 regression test (passes). The 'rerun with the pilot paid' that the README's own limitation calls for has not been done. Everything the README says is done works: 3.
evidence.verification: `PYTHONPATH=src python3.13 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 7 tests OK. Four seeded mutants via platform/ci/quality_mutate.py: window doubled in late_loss_usd (fleet.py:81) SURVIVED; inline labour SETUP_GROUND -> SETUP_SCOUT (fleet.py:104, every inline cost) SURVIVED; inline tie-break reversed to most machines (fleet.py:126) SURVIVED; removing the scout->treater precedence max() (fleet.py:53) caught. 3 of 4 survive, including the core lateness comparison; no test touches inline_total, best_inline or run.py, which produce every headline: 1.
evidence.craft: Read fleet.py (130 lines), run.py, figure.py, test_fleet.py, and diffed fleet.py against osrobot-deadline's. Small and readable, constants named and marked ASSUMED. Defects: fleet.py is a verbatim copy of osrobot-deadline's (itself copied from osrobot-pipeline), so the pilot fix in osrobot-pairprice did not reach it; run.py:8 and :12 print '\\n' (double-escaped) so the README's reproduce command writes literal backslash-n into results.txt, meaning the committed file was not produced by the committed script; inline search runs n to 32 for 16 fields (n>16 is dead work); no interval or sensitivity on the fitted lines. 2.
evidence.claims: Checked: every number in the four README bullets against results.txt and my re-implementation (all match); Knezevic 2003 2% per leaf stage and its canopy-closure limit (matches the abstract); 'no new simulation' (true, fitted lines); '7 tests, under a second' (true); 'Builds on' 13.92 (true). But the README headlines (README.md:9-10) and the live page lede/summary (project.json:4-5) state that at 1.62 ha the pipeline is cheaper from a 12 h window and that the parent verdict 'mostly survives', while README.md:41 says the scout pilot is unpaid and results where the scout fleet wins are conditional; project.json carries no such caveat. With the pilot paid the pipeline loses in every cell (2.25-2.71 at 1.62 ha). A served headline the repository itself knows is reversed: 1.
evidence.fitness: A researcher cannot build on the finding: (1) pilot unpaid, already corrected upstream on 2026-11-14 but not rerun here; (2) held-fleet capital is charged as total_cap * 0.30 * makespan_h / 500 (fleet.py:86-87), i.e. per machine-hour, so buying 16 robots to finish in 6 h costs the same as 1 robot over 99 h: the peak-capacity cost that a deadline study exists to price is zero, and the only penalty for more machines is pipeline imbalance; (3) no prior work is cited for the method: timeliness cost (yield value * coefficient * days late) is the standard ASABE EP496/D497 machinery-selection practice, and fleet sizing against due dates with tardiness cost is a classic hybrid flow-shop problem; (4) not part of a programme in research/PROGRAMMES.md as far as the README says. The idea (replace a hard deadline with a sourced timeliness loss) is sensible and the code is a usable stub: 1.
evidence.domain: Compared against farm-machinery management practice (ASABE EP496.3 timeliness cost, D497 coefficients; annual ownership cost per machine when sizing a fleet for a seasonal window) and real-time scheduling practice (tardiness-weighted cost, capacity cost for meeting deadlines). The lateness model is the right shape and the 2% per leaf stage rate is correctly sourced and limited (applied linearly, capped at 100%, validity to canopy closure stated). Departures a reviewer would flag first: fixed ownership cost replaced by per-hour use cost, which removes the cost of capacity; scout pilot labour omitted contrary to 14 CFR 107.31; lateness counted in working hours while machines are scheduled continuously, with no daily calendar; one window for all fields. 1.

defects.what: Scout pilot's flight minutes are not charged (14 CFR 107.31 visual line of sight), a defect already fixed upstream in osrobot-pairprice on 2026-11-14. With the pilot paid at the project's 20 USD/h the pipeline costs 2.25-2.71 times inline at 1.62 ha in every cell, so the headline 'at 1.62 ha the verdict flips with the window' and 'verdict mostly survives' do not hold.
Live page lede and summary state the 1.62 ha flip (pipeline cheaper from 12 h) with no pilot caveat, although the README's own limitation says such results are conditional on an unpaid pilot.

Held-fleet capital is charged per machine-hour of makespan (total_cap*0.30*h/500), so n inline robots cost the same for any n dividing 16 (12.27 USD/ha for n=1..16 at 1.62 ha). The capacity cost of meeting a tight window, the quantity a deadline study must price, is zero; the 'lateness costs little' finding is largely this artefact.

Tests miss the core: doubling the window in late_loss_usd, changing every inline labour cost, and reversing the inline tie-break all leave the 7 tests green; inline_total, best_inline and run.py are untested.

No prior work cited for the method: ASABE EP496/D497 timeliness-cost coefficients (the standard yield-times-days-late form this reimplements), hybrid flow-shop scheduling with weighted tardiness, or robot-weeding economics (Lowenberg-DeBoer et al. 2020); novelty is unstated.
run.py prints double-escaped '\\n', so the README reproduce command writes literal backslash-n into results.txt; the committed results.txt was not produced by the committed script.
fleet.py is a third-generation verbatim copy (osrobot-pipeline -> osrobot-deadline -> here), so upstream fixes such as the pilot charge do not propagate.

verdict: Small, readable and arithmetically exact: every number in the README and results.txt reproduces in an independent re-implementation and by hand, and the 2% per leaf stage loss rate is correctly sourced and limited. But it computes a model the repository already knows is wrong. The scout pilot is unpaid, a defect fixed upstream in osrobot-pairprice six days before this audit; with the pilot paid the scout-and-treater fleet costs 2.25 to 2.71 times inline in every 1.62 ha cell, so the headline flip at 1.62 ha disappears, while the live page lede still states it without a caveat. Capital charged per machine-hour makes extra robots free, which removes the capacity cost a deadline study exists to price. Three of four seeded mutants survive, including doubling the window, and no timeliness-cost or scheduling prior work is cited. Finished as described (completeness 3), below the bar on correctness, claims and verification.
